newsitem.title: ITALY: FORECAST-Italy December CPI seen stable at 2.6 pct.
newsitem.headline: FORECAST-Italy December CPI seen stable at 2.6 pct.

text.p: Italy's preliminary December annual consumer price index (CPI) inflation is seen stable from last month with a slight increase forecast on a monthly basis, a Reuter poll of 12 analysts showed on Tuesday.

Analysts on average saw inflation rising by 0.1 percent month-on-month and 2.6 percent annually, after 0.3 percent and 2.6 percent increases in November. In December 1995, on the basis of an old index, prices rose 0.2 percent and 5.8 percent respectively.

Ten Italian sample cities will publish their preliminary December CPI inflation data on December 19 and 20 at around 1630 GMT, while Italy's national statistics body ISTAT will release the national data for December on January 8.
Italy's Treasury minister Carlo Azeglio Ciampi said on Tuesday that he saw inflation in the coming months levelling out at around November's 2.6 percent level.
Analysts noted that in December there was little significant price pressure and inflation was still generally on a downward track, but there is more uncertainty over the January data.
"There could be details of indirect tax measures which could contribute to a rise in inflation in January and maybe even in February," said Pio de Gregorio, analyst at NatWest in Milan.
Analysts attribute the slight rise in the monthly figure to average price increases in many CPI components, counterbalanced by a weak economy which is affecting consumption.

"There will be a price hike in home goods and recreation goods because of Christmas but this will be counterbalanced by sales in other components especially in the food sector, and a weak economic cycle which limits consumption," said Alfredo Granata, analyst at Banca di Roma.

"Only apparel (clothing), and hotel and restaurant services' prices should have risen above the overall average. Food prices are likely to have remained subdued, continuing the trend of recent months," investment bank JP Morgan said in a note.
